newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH sees little impact on HK business.
newsitem.headline: LVMH sees little impact on HK business.

text.p: LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton said on Tuesday that the failure of its DFS subsidiary to win the two principal concessions at Hong Kong's new airport would have only a "marginal" impact on DFS's business in Hong Kong.
"LVMH recalls that more than 70 percent of DFS's turnover is generated outside airports. DFS's development strategy aims to raise that percentage significantly," LVMH said in a statement.
It added that, at the prices paid for the concessions, it would not have been able to operate them profitably.
LVMH's stock fell sharply on Tuesday on news DFS had not obtained the concessions for the new Chep Lap Kok airport that would have replaced the concessions it held at the old airport.
The share was down 3.9 percent at 1,430 francs at 1415 GMT, underperforming the CAC which was down 1.8 percent.

LVMH said DFS opened a large downtown outlet last year and was renovating its other outlet in central Hong Kong. "The loss of the existing concession should therefore have only a very marginal effect on the group's business in Hong Kong," it said.
"Furthermore, DFS notes that the offers made by its competitors, far superior to its own, would not have allowed it to operate the concessions with a positive margin," it said.
LVMH acquired control of San Francisco-based Duty Free Shoppers in January for $2.6 billion.
